note: Move slowly and breathe through the nose. Hold times are for building up gently: start with Beginner. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or breathlessness. If you are pregnant, recovering from surgery or have a heart, blood-pressure or other medical condition, check with your doctor first.

steps.name: 1. Pranamasana (Prayer Pose)
steps.text: Stand erect, palms joined at chest in namaskar mudra
steps.meaning: Salutations to Mitra, the friend of all beings

steps.name: 2. Hasta Uttanasana (Raised Arms Pose)
steps.text: Raise arms overhead, arch back, stretch whole body
steps.meaning: Salutations to Ravi, the shining one who causes change

steps.name: 3. Pada Hastasana (Standing Forward Bend)
steps.text: Bend forward from hips, hands beside feet, forehead toward knees
steps.meaning: Salutations to Surya, the dispeller of darkness who inspires noble deeds

steps.name: 4. Ashwa Sanchalanasana (Equestrian Pose)
steps.text: Step right leg back, left foot between hands, look up
steps.meaning: Salutations to Bhanu, the one who illuminates and enlightens

steps.name: 5. Dandasana (Plank Pose)
steps.text: Step left leg back, body straight, arms perpendicular to floor
steps.meaning: Salutations to Khaga, the one who moves through the sky

steps.name: 6. Ashtanga Namaskara (Eight-Limbed Salutation)
steps.text: Lower knees, chest and chin to floor; eight limbs touch ground
steps.meaning: Salutations to Pushan, the one who nourishes and gives strength

steps.name: 7. Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose)
steps.text: Slide forward, raise chest, arch back, look up
steps.meaning: Salutations to Hiranyagarbha, the golden cosmic womb that contains all

steps.name: 8. Adho Mukha Shvanasana (Downward-Facing Dog Pose)
steps.text: Lift hips up and back, heels toward floor, form inverted V
steps.meaning: Salutations to Marichi, the one who possesses rays of light and creates positive waves

steps.name: 9. Ashwa Sanchalanasana (Equestrian Pose)
steps.text: Step right leg forward between hands, look up
steps.meaning: Salutations to Aditya, the supreme son of Aditi, the infinite mother

steps.name: 10. Pada Hastasana (Standing Forward Bend)
steps.text: Bring left foot forward beside right, bend forward
steps.meaning: Salutations to Savitri, the one who is the source of everything

steps.name: 11. Hasta Uttanasana (Raised Arms Pose)
steps.text: Rise up, arms overhead, arch back
steps.meaning: Salutations to Arka, the one who is worthy of praise and worship

steps.name: 12. Pranamasana (Prayer Pose)
steps.text: Bring palms together at chest in prayer position, stand erect
steps.meaning: Salutations to Bhaskara, the one who leads to enlightenment and is the cause of light and knowledge

how: Twelve poses linked with the breath; one round leads with the right leg, the next with the left.
Beginner holds each pose for 8 seconds; Advanced flows at 4 seconds a pose.

Each pose shows its mantra, meaning and breath. The opening verse comes first; after the last round the closing verse, Bhaskara Stotram, Surya Ashtakam, Guru Namaskara and Dheerga Danda Namaskara follow, one verse per page.
Follow the pose name and cue on screen; keep the movements smooth.
items.caution: Skip the back-bend if you have a back injury. Avoid in late pregnancy.

how: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart, weight even on both feet.
Lengthen the spine, relax the shoulders, arms by the sides.
Breathe slowly and feel the body stand tall and steady.
Stand on the left leg. Place the right foot on the inner calf or thigh (never on the knee).
Bring the palms together at the chest or overhead.
Fix the gaze on one point and breathe evenly. Change legs.
items.caution: Use a wall if balance is unsteady.

how: Step the feet wide; turn the right foot out.
Reach to the right and lower the right hand to the shin or a block; raise the left arm.
Keep both legs straight and the chest open. Change sides.
items.caution: Keep the neck neutral if it feels strained.

how: Step the feet wide, right foot out, left foot slightly in.
Bend the right knee over the ankle; stretch the arms out at shoulder height.
Look over the right hand; keep the torso upright. Change sides.
items.caution: Keep the knee over the ankle, not past the toes.

how: Lie on the front with hands under the shoulders, legs together.
Breathe in and lift the chest, elbows slightly bent, hips on the floor.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears; lower down as you breathe out.
items.caution: Avoid with a recent back injury or in pregnancy.

how: Lie on the back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart near the hips.
Press into the feet and lift the hips; arms rest on the floor.
Breathe steadily, then roll down slowly.
items.caution: Do not turn the head while in the pose.
items.benefit: Opens the chest, strengthens legs and back.

how: From hands and knees, lift the hips up and back into an inverted V.
Spread the fingers, press the floor away, heels reaching down.
Bend the knees as much as needed to keep the back long.
items.caution: Avoid with uncontrolled high blood pressure or a wrist injury.
items.benefit: Stretches the back of the body.

how: Kneel, sit back on the heels and fold forward.
Rest the forehead on the mat, arms forward or beside the body.
Breathe into the back; rest here whenever you need.
items.caution: Place a cushion between the hips and heels if the knees hurt.

how: Sit with the legs straight in front.
Breathe in to lengthen; breathe out and fold from the hips, reaching for the shins or feet.
Keep the back long rather than rounding; use a strap around the feet.
items.caution: Bend the knees if the lower back pulls.

how: Kneel and sit on the heels, big toes touching.
Hands on the thighs, spine tall, breathe slowly.
Traditionally practised after meals to aid digestion.
Come to hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe in, let the belly drop and look up (cow).
Breathe out, round the back and tuck the chin (cat). Keep flowing.
Lie on the back, legs apart, arms away from the body, palms up.
Close the eyes and let the whole body become heavy.
Breathe naturally. End every session here.
